deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the manuscript title page of a notebook (Gauss's 'Handbuch 2'), lettered in calligraphic Roman capitals: 'OPVSCVLA / VARII ARGVMENTI / VOLVMEN PRIMVM / [rule] / BRVNOVICI 1800.' This translates as 'Small works on various subjects, Volume one, Braunschweig 1800.'

Later additions:
- A library shelfmark in pencil at top right, 'Handb 2', with the folio number '1.' beside it.
- The purple stamp of the Niedersächsische Staats- und Universitätsbibliothek Göttingen.
- A short pencil note at the foot of the page, written upside down relative to the title. It appears to begin '9 Mai' (or '9 May'); the rest is illegible to me.

The date and place fit Gauss's Braunschweig period, when he was writing up results in notebooks of this kind. The neighbouring pages are the bundle's cover and accession notes (the previous page) and miscellaneous practical notes on a coin diameter, room height and gold-balance weights (the next page). Those are later entries; none of their content belongs to this page.

There is no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Title page of a Gauss notebook: 'Opuscula varii argumenti, Volumen primum, Brunovici 1800' (Handbuch 2)
results.usually_credited_to: Carl Friedrich Gauss (notebook known in the Gauss Nachlass, Göttingen, as Handbuch 2)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a title page with no mathematical content. Gauss's Braunschweig-period notebooks ('Handbücher') are catalogued and known in the literature, so nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: The calligraphy uses V for U throughout: 'OPVSCVLA', 'ARGVMENTI', 'VOLVMEN PRIMVM', 'BRVNOVICI' (the transcription normalized these to U).
'VARII' is written with a long final i, appearing as 'VARIJ'.
'Handb 2' at top right is a pencil shelfmark (Handbuch 2) added later, with the folio number '1.' beside it.
The bottom pencil note is upside down. It seems to begin '9 Mai' (or '9 May'), but the remainder is illegible and the reading is uncertain.
A horizontal rule separates 'VOLVMEN PRIMVM' and the stamp from the imprint line 'BRVNOVICI 1800.'
